title: bonsai.line/1
description: bonsai status --line --json (spec §4; contract §12; plan-5 5.6.0 and 5.6.4): the statusline's workspace half as fields, with the line itself, so a studio's statusline draws it its own way and a plain one prints line. Cheap and offline, like status --json; printed, never stored. Written by bonsai status --line with --json; read by the studio's statusline and agents. Outside a linked folder it is not an error: workspace and task are null and line is "". A writer writes every field below, in this order, null or [] where it does not apply (contract §2.2); a reader treats a missing field as null, keeps an unknown one and refuses a duplicate key.

format.description: The version, always the first field (contract §2.2).

workspace.description: The workspace's id and name from bonsai.yaml; null when the folder is not linked.

task.description: The active task (contract §13): its id, title and status; null when there is none.

title.description: The task's title, as its file has it.

status.description: The task's status, as its file has it (bonsai.task/1's status).

running.description: How many tasks read running when no one task is active (none, or two or more); null when one is active, or the folder is not linked.

ladder.description: Where the active task's proof stands, a closed list: green (its last result is green at this checkout's HEAD), red (red at HEAD), old (its last result is for another commit), none (no result yet); null with no active task.

verify.description: How many tasks read verify; 0 when the folder is not linked.

asks.description: How many asks are open (bonsai.asks/1 lists them); 0 when the folder is not linked.

release.description: A newer Bonsai release's version, as the home's last read of the releases found it (status --json's bonsai_release); null when none is newer, or none was read.

line.description: The line itself, one line of ASCII as status --line prints it without --json; "" when the folder is not linked.
examples: example T-0901 running ladder green verify 1

error.description: null unless the command refused or failed: then what went wrong and the next step, as bonsai.error has it.

examples.message: bonsai.yaml is not in this checkout, so it is not linked to Bonsai

next.do: run: bonsai init in the project's main checkout

code.description: What went wrong, as a fixed word: an open list (contract §2.2). Later steps add words, which is an addition (format review 4.5), and a reader shows a word it does not know as other. The known words live in one table in Bonsai's code, their one home, which bonsai check --schema bonsai.error prints (and, from step 5.1.10, the reference page of lists, docs/reference/lists.md); this schema does not copy them, and the words in its examples are illustrative.

message.description: What is wrong, one sentence for a person, in ASCII (spec §3).
examples: no --yes, and no terminal to ask at: nothing was written

next.description: The next thing to do (spec §3: every refusal and error names it, in the human line and in the JSON): what to do and who does it.

do.description: What to do: the command to run, written run: and the command line, or the step in plain words.
examples: open Claude Code in this checkout and accept its trust question

who.description: Who does it, a closed list: agent (any agent may do it, unattended) or person (a person's step: a consent such as --allow-exec, a tap, a setting, an install, or a command an agent's task does not grant it; spec §4, §6).
